title: Container Traffic at Major Ports (TEU)
description: Containers handled by the 12 Major (government-owned) ports each month, in thousand twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU), from the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways' monthly cargo reports. Container volumes track manufactured goods trade (exports of engineering goods, textiles, chemicals and imports of electronics and machinery) more closely than bulk cargo, so this complements the Port Cargo Traffic page, which is total tonnes dominated by coal, crude oil and iron ore.
source: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Cargo handled at Major Ports (monthly)

qna.question: What does this series measure?
qna.answer: Total containers handled (loaded and discharged, imports, exports, transhipment and coastal) at India's 12 Major Ports, expressed in TEU - a 20-foot container is 1 TEU, a 40-foot container 2. The unit here is thousand TEU.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: It is a physical indicator of merchandise trade in manufactured goods. Use year-on-year growth: seasonality is moderate (peaks around Oct-Mar, with export shipping ahead of the holiday season), and shipping disruptions (Red Sea diversions, port congestion) can shift volumes between months or between major and non-major ports.^Compare with the exports and imports values on the Trade pages: container volume growth above value growth suggests falling unit values.

qna.question: What are the caveats?
qna.answer: Coverage is the 12 Major Ports only; private non-major ports (notably Mundra) handle a large and growing share of containers, so share shifts can move this series independently of trade. The latest month is an 'advance estimate' compared with provisional estimates of the previous year, and the Ministry revises figures in later reports.^Pre-2024 reports gave TEU in thousands (rounded), so earlier history is slightly coarser.

note: 12 Major Ports only (Mundra, Pipavav and other non-major ports are excluded, so this is not all-India container traffic; JNPA and Deendayal are the largest). Latest month is an advance estimate. Each month's figure is the one in its own report, replaced by the revised year-ago figure printed in the following year's report. Reports before 2024 give TEU rounded to the nearest thousand.
